issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath N1 §6.1.1 Equality, Quantity Equality, Date/Time Equality; §6.1.3 Not Equals
issues.evidence: Fresh probe `.temp/qa/fp13_historian_probe.py` showed native C++ returns false/true for ordered multi-item equality/inequality when a paired singleton comparison is empty. Repro: `(@2012 | @2013) = (@2012-01 | @2013)` native `[false]`/False vs fallback empty/NULL; `(1 'cm' | 2 'cm') = (1 'g' | 2 'cm')` native `[false]`/False vs fallback empty/NULL. Expected empty because Date/Time precision mismatch and incompatible Quantity dimensions make the paired singleton equality indeterminate; `!=` is `(=).not()` and also empty.
issues.root_cause: Native ordered multi-item equality reused Boolean-only fpValuesEqual(), which cannot represent singleton equality returning empty for Date/Time precision mismatch, timezone indeterminacy, incompatible Quantity dimensions, or other incompatible singleton pairs.
issues.resolution: Added native tri-state singleton equality evaluation for ordered multi-item `=`/`!=`; it returns empty for indeterminate paired comparisons and only collapses to Boolean for true/false pairs. Added parity and native sqllogictest regressions.
issues.verified_in: `.temp/qa/fp13_historian_probe_after_fix.log` 47/47 clean; `pytest test_equality_parity.py` 8 passed; native sqllogictest 548 assertions; full conformance 2822/2822.

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath N1 §6.1.2 Equivalent and Complex Type Equivalence
issues.evidence: Fresh probe `.temp/qa/fp13_historian_probe.py` showed forced Python fallback returns empty/NULL for `objA ~ objB` and `objA !~ objB` when equivalent complex objects contain list-valued child properties with complex elements in different order; native returns true/false. stderr shows `TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'dict' and 'dict'`. Expected complex equivalence to recurse through child equivalence and compare multi-item collections order-independently.
issues.root_cause: Forced Python fallback complex equivalence sorted child lists directly; Python cannot order dict elements, so recursive equivalence over list-valued complex child properties raised TypeError and public UDFs returned empty/NULL.
issues.resolution: Replaced direct sorting with recursive order-independent matching for list-valued complex children and routed numeric child comparison through existing FHIRPath equivalence rounding. Added parity coverage for nested complex child lists.
issues.verified_in: `.temp/qa/fp13_historian_probe_after_fix.log` 47/47 clean; `pytest test_equality_parity.py` 8 passed; native sqllogictest 548 assertions; full conformance 2822/2822.
